key_insight: Early pregnancy HbA1c alone shows only modest ability to identify later gestational diabetes in low- and middle-income country cohorts, with better performance at high or low cutoffs than at a single threshold.
clinical_relevance: HbA1c could help triage pregnant patients for further testing when OGTT access is difficult, but it should not replace OGTT for diagnosis.
method: Prospective multisite cohort of 10,918 pregnancies enrolled before 20 weeks in Kenya, India, Pakistan, and Zambia
Measured HbA1c early in pregnancy and compared it with later GDM diagnosed by IADPSG OGTT criteria
Assessed prediction using ROC/AUC plus single- and two-threshold approaches, and linked HbA1c to pregnancy outcomes with regression and meta-analysis
evidence_signal: HbA1c alone had an AUC of 0.65 for predicting GDM; a 5.4% single cutoff had limited sensitivity and specificity, while 5.0% and 5.5% cutoffs improved rule-out and rule-in performance respectively.
watch_item: HbA1c performance was only moderate, so implementation could miss cases or over-triage patients if used without confirmatory OGTT.
paper_title: Early Pregnancy Glycosylated Hemoglobin in Relation to Gestational Diabetes Mellitus and Adverse Pregnancy Outcomes: Evidence from a Multisite Low- and Middle-Income Countries Cohort
